QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_57

question.text: For an open-ended Cat III AIF with called capital INR 50 cr, NAV (pre-incentives) at end of Y2 INR 63.30 cr, HWM INR 56.42 cr, Reference Hurdle INR 60.50 cr, incentive fee rate 15%. Incentive fee:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ex 9.3: Minimum NAV eligible for incentive = higher of (HWM 56.42, Hurdle 60.50) = 60.50 cr. Excess = 63.30 − 60.50 = 2.80 cr. Incentive = 15% × 2.80 = INR 0.4199 crore (approx INR 42 lakh). (Using the exact Ex 9.3 figure: 63.2995 − 60.50 = 2.7995 × 15% = 0.4199 cr.) The Trap: Option A is the excess amount itself (before incentive %). Option C uses HWM as threshold. Option D is mis-stated magnitude. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B tests HWM+hurdle combined; XIX-C requires reconciliation. Manager's Pro-Tip: When Reference Hurdle > HWM (as here), the hurdle is the binding constraint — LPs benefit. When HWM > Hurdle (after a strong year), HWM binds. Model both regimes in your incentive fee accrual system.
